title: SpaceX credit risk jumps on worries over its borrowing spree
key_facts: SpaceX is in talks with banks and investors to raise $40 billion (about 54 trillion won) to buy Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI computing platform.
The article calls it the largest debt deal ever for AI infrastructure.
Five-year credit default swaps on SpaceX debt rose as much as 16.7 basis points to about 197.6 basis points, an all-time high for the credit risk gauge, according to ICE Data Services.
SpaceX's 5.875% notes due 2036 widened 5 basis points to 193 basis points on the day, according to Trace.
Those notes were at 140 basis points when issued in June as part of a $25 billion debt deal.
Meta Platforms' 6.45% notes due 2066 also widened 5 basis points, to 189 basis points.
quote_evidence: As a result, the gauge of SpaceX's credit risk has jumped to an all-time high.
It would be the largest debt deal ever for AI infrastructure.
Concern over the heavy borrowing is spreading to the bond market.
why_it_matters_hint: Lenders and bondholders are asking more for the risk of lending to SpaceX, while the $40 billion deal is still in talks.
